title: macOS native browser session discovery
acceptance: Clean macOS login, refresh and encrypted-session diagnosis without a legacy session or XDG workaround.

title: Frozen provider watermark strands the vector drain
acceptance: Bounded recovery with no externally invented provider mutation; exact generation and delete-absence proofs still required.

title: Completed bootstrap history, delayed visibility and overlapping retries
acceptance: Complete a real bootstrap, add, overwrite and delete corpus rows, interrupt and resume with historical batch rows and delayed provider visibility; pass every intermediate Worker receipt through the actual CLI validators, including deletion alone and deletion to an empty corpus, then verify exact reconciliation.

title: Whole-corpus pause and safe recovery availability
acceptance: Prove a bounded, documented recovery journey for a large paused corpus; do not unpause manually or promise active background bootstrap before it exists. Every operator-facing description of the update and recovery order must match the endpoints: bootstrap answers 409 unless VECTOR_DRAIN_MODE=paused-for-upgrade, and drain and reindex answer 503 while that pause holds, so no documented order may unpause before it reprojects.

title: Authentication formats, refresh and account selection
acceptance: Exercise browser, account token, revoked token, expiry, conflicting environment identity and two-account selection on supported hosts.

title: Windows CLI identity, MSIX paths and PowerShell shims
acceptance: Resolve actual executable and version before and after installing into one prefix; run pasted commands with restrictive PowerShell and redirected APPDATA. Verify every printed human command uses the actual installed executable; require physical Windows and ARM64 acceptance before closure.

title: Source boundaries and exclusions
acceptance: Mixed-source destructive requests and all-except grants cannot cross exclusions before, during or after upgrade.

title: Passkeys, revocation, consent and single-use state
acceptance: Physical owner ceremony plus concurrent consume, failed retry, final-owner guard, both consent actions and session revocation.

title: Financial cursor and completeness claims
acceptance: Reject incomplete provider pages without advancing cursors; omitted, explicit, boundary and above-boundary limits and visible-row totals agree. Prove provider record-lock custody; destination sharing still needs independent acceptance.

title: Exact package publication only after every gate
acceptance: Before publication: one tested package, six completed OS/Node jobs, planted traps, reviewed field evidence, immutable releases enabled and a verified enforcing workflow; no release before CI finishes. After publication, verify immutable tag and asset bytes before URL promotion.

title: Recovery evidence and D1 versus Vectorize restoration
acceptance: Disposable restore rehearsal preserves authoritative documents and rebuilds derived vectors; no live D1 export or bookmark-first recovery.

title: Windows ARM64 Node 24 physical runtime
acceptance: Run actual packaged CLI, DPAPI, login, update interruption and normal process exit on Windows ARM64 Node 24; x64 hosted CI is insufficient.

deferral.reason: The acceptance requires a physical Windows ARM64 host on Node 24 and states in its own text that x64 hosted CI is insufficient, so no CI run can ever close it. No ARM64 machine exists on the bench, and 0.4.0 does not claim Windows ARM64 as a supported runtime.
deferral.unproven: Windows ARM64 owners get no packaged-launch, DPAPI, browser login, interrupted-update or clean-exit proof in 0.4.0. The release note must name Windows x64 as the only claimed Windows runtime.

title: Actual setup wrapper and repeat-setup behavior
acceptance: Exercise the actual packed CLI with missing manifest and existing active install; error remedies must not re-pause a working Brain.

title: Honest health, version and retrieval handoff
acceptance: Record executable/package/manifest/worker/D1 versions separately; verify ingestion, paused state, backlog trend and cited retrieval, never infer recovery from HTTP 200.

title: Runbook, prerequisites and connector scope match the package
acceptance: Reconcile historical install-log sections 1, 3-7 with exact packaged commands, paid-plan failure point, supported connectors, approved folder and mail scopes, taxpayer-ID limits, deduplication, real retrieval questions and owner handoff. Unavailable sources must remain explicit.

title: Interrupted provisioning, schedules and durable credential pointers
acceptance: Interrupt each setup stage; retry an already-correct schedule; ensure manifest credential pointers resolve durably and deploy/status/source commands discover the same authorized credential. No remedy loops back into a needless pause.

title: Plaid configuration survives install, deploy and update
acceptance: Verify the exact packaged CLI deploys the named sandbox/production profile, required independent wrapping key, country selection and reconciliation interval; actual disposable Worker configuration and callback must be read back.

deferral.reason: The acceptance requires a real, live Plaid Item against a real institution with real accounts, and its own text excludes API-only Sandbox receipts and CI. No live Item exists for this cut because general bank invitations remain closed, which is what the Plaid release gate means by held. The deferral holds only while they stay closed.
deferral.unproven: Plaid configuration survives install, deploy and update is unproven against a real Worker with a real Item; only the packaged CLI's configuration read-back is exercised.

acceptance: Prove same-session replay, concurrent new sessions, existing Item reauthorization, ambiguous same-bank accounts and retained disconnected history do not create duplicate balances or history; changed provider identities require explicit continuity review, never automatic matching from a name or mask.

acceptance: Prove at least four Items make progress when earlier Items await assignment or fail; overlapping cron/manual slices and expired owners cannot overwrite staging, promote or advance another run cursor.

title: Plaid complete owner journey and financial entity setup
acceptance: Before invitations, verify the exact disposable deployed candidate with two institutions and four accounts assigned to one person and two businesses, including adding missing entities, initial and later sync, balances, webhook delivery, scheduled fallback, reauthorization and confirmed disconnect with retained history. Record Mac and Windows owner browser journeys separately, then an approved production pilot. API-only Sandbox receipts or CI do not close this gate.

title: Windows Google credential storage uses the current shared encryption helper
acceptance: On each supported Windows runtime, run the source and exact installed package gates: 25 DPAPI round trips, one helper compilation, admin-key create/read/rotate and Google credential save/read. Verify captured helper identity, 65 successful invocations, no plaintext or metadata disclosure, and clean normal exit. Then prove sign-in and refresh in the owner field journey. A passing injected PowerShell test cannot stand in for the production bridge.

title: Owner uploads and private access links stay bound to their entity and recipient
acceptance: In the actual owner components on Mac and Windows, stage a file under A and switch to B, whole-Brain, and back to A. No file or retry identity may transfer without a fresh selection. Delay file reads, searches and grant responses across scope, recipient and selection changes; stale completions must not repopulate another context, enable an old private-link copy action, clear a new draft, or refresh the wrong entity. Preserve correctly submitted original-entity requests and backend cross-entity refusal. Verify the rebuilt packaged owner page before field acceptance.

title: Bank freshness never reports a failed or unfetched refresh as current
acceptance: With a real Item, prove the owner is never told current while a refresh is actually owed. A saved ready snapshot must not inherit a later webhook's history without fetching it, and a ready or interrupted-prefix resume must publish its exact saved data while staying partial and immediately due. A refresh that fails, including one that fails before any provider read such as an unreadable access reference, must show as refresh debt in both the owner account inventory and the feed status, not merely in needs_attention. An ordinary future scheduled poll on an actually fetched feed must still read current, and the debt must clear once a real refresh succeeds. Repeat across two institutions and at least four accounts spanning personal and two businesses, including a real business banking login, with a verified signed webhook and a deliberately missed notification recovered on schedule.

deferral.reason: The acceptance requires a real, live Plaid Item against a real institution with real accounts, and its own text excludes API-only Sandbox receipts and CI. No live Item exists for this cut because general bank invitations remain closed, which is what the Plaid release gate means by held. The deferral holds only while they stay closed.
deferral.unproven: That an owner is never told current while a refresh is owed is unproven with a real Item and real webhook history.

title: Windows release evidence comes from a verified package on a proven runtime
acceptance: Every Windows lane must start the main test chain rather than failing on command-line length, and no step that installs or runs the packaged bytes may execute unless the exact-package checksum step succeeded. Continuation after an unrelated source test failure must be preserved. Assert runner architecture and Node platform, architecture and major before install, and feed every lane from one exact artifact. Diagnose the Node 22 first-install timeout from the sanitized diagnostics before changing any timeout; correlation with an npm or Node version is not a cause. The all-ref history privacy gate remains a separate release blocker and must not be waived.

title: Public rate-limit policies defined but never wired to their routes
acceptance: Every route class the public request guard defines a policy for must call the guard before its handler runs, and each guarded handler must read the request the guard returns rather than the original, whose body the guard has already bounded. Prove on a deployed brain that an anonymous request to each public class is refused once its policy limit is exceeded, and that a refusal is returned rather than a durable write. The owner-facing consequence this closes is that an anonymous caller who learns a brain's hostname could drive unmetered writes into the owner's own paid database.

title: The workers.dev subdomain read blamed an account setting for a credential failure
acceptance: Reading the account subdomain must report which of three things went wrong: no credential was available for that call, the read was attempted and refused, or the read succeeded and the subdomain really is unset. A credential failure must reach the operator with its own text intact, including its warning against pasting a token into a shell, and must never be relabelled as a missing account setting. Prove on a deployed install driven by a browser session, with no API token in the environment, that the failing path names the credential rather than the subdomain, and that an operator following the message is never led to change a setting that is already correct.

title: Adoption on a name match let a second install take the first brain
acceptance: Two installs into one provider account must never resolve to the same brain, and adoption of an existing database or vector index must require that the manifest already recorded owning it rather than that a name or a client slug happens to match. Prove on a deployed account that a second install from a fresh manifest is refused by name for both the database and the vector index, that it creates and adopts nothing, and that the manifest which provisioned those resources can still re-run and adopt them. The failure this closes was observed end to end on 2026-09-08: two independent manifests both resolved to one brain, the second reported adopting it and reusing its durable admin key, and from the second manifest the first install's corpus was listable.
findings: Proved on a deployed provider account on 2026-09-08 against commit 8393c20 packaged as brain-installer-0.4.2.tgz. A second install from a fresh manifest was refused on the database, created nothing, and left the account inventory unchanged. Claiming the database by hand, which is the repair the refusal names, then hit a second refusal on the vector index, so each resource is guarded on its own record of ownership rather than on one gate. The owning manifest re-ran and adopted both, query-ready. Ownership is now written to the manifest as each resource is created, before the roughly nine-minute metadata-index wait, so an interrupted install no longer strands its own owner.

title: The Windows release gate failed on runner speed rather than on the code
acceptance: The owner-scope browser suite must decide on behaviour, never on how fast the runner happens to be, because a gate that fails at random teaches the release to ignore it. Observed on 2026-09-08 at commit 20dbbc7d: the identical commit passed the full windows-latest node 22 job on its push run and failed the same job on its pull_request run, in document-access.browser.mjs, waiting ten seconds for a button that six earlier pages in the same file had already rendered. The harness ran a Vite dev server that compiles modules on demand and re-runs its dependency optimizer the first time it meets an unbundled import, and it held every assertion to a ten-second desktop ceiling while two shared cores ran Chromium, that server and esbuild together. Prove the fix by running the suite on each supported platform, on a cold cache, and confirming that both files report every check passed, that no assertion is the first thing to compile a fixture, and that a genuine regression still fails. A real defect fails at any ceiling, so a longer shared-runner ceiling removes no coverage.
findings: The flake had two independent halves and both are closed. The harness now loads every fixture once before the caller starts asserting, so module compilation and dependency optimisation are paid off the clock instead of in the middle of a test. Separately, the per-assertion ceiling is now 45 seconds on a shared runner and stays at 10 seconds on a developer machine, overridable through BRAIN_BROWSER_TIMEOUT_MS. Locally the two files complete 32 checks in under ten seconds including the warm-up.
